title: Apply for a high risk work licence
summary: This page explains how to apply for a high risk work (HRW) licence or an added class online if you have received a notice of satisfactory assessment (NSA).
intro:
If you have been sent your notice of satisfactory assessment (NSA), you can complete your application for a high risk work (HRW) licence or added class online.

You must apply for your licence within 60 days of the date your NSA was issued.
who_can_apply: Have completed HRW training with a registered training organisation (RTO) in the appropriate class or classes.
Have been assessed as competent in the class by a SafeWork NSW accredited assessor working for the RTO and been sent your Notice of Satisfactory Assessment (NSA).
Be able to use English at a level that enables high risk work to be carried out safely.
what_you_need: Your current HRW licence (if you have one).
Two documents from List 1, or one document from List 1 and one document from List 2.
Australian certificate of registration by descent.
Aviation and Maritime Security Identification card.
Proof of identity documents (details from 2 identity documents are required, at least one must be a photo ID).
If your name has changed due to marriage or divorce, you may need a document that links your name, such as a marriage certificate.

how_to_steps.text: Log in to your MyService NSW account.
Follow the prompts to submit your application.
You'll get a confirmation email and receipt after you submit your application.
You may be required to visit a Service NSW Centre to have your photo taken.
You'll get your licence in the post.

more_info.text: To find your high risk work licence number and details, visit Verify NSW.
Find help and information about MyServiceNSW Accounts.

faqs.q: How long do I have to apply for my HRW licence?
faqs.a: You must apply for your licence within 60 days of the date your Notice of Satisfactory Assessment (NSA) was issued.

faqs.q: What do I need to apply for the licence?
faqs.a: You need a MyServiceNSW Account, your current HRW licence (if applicable), fee payment, and specific identity documents.

faqs.q: Do I need to visit a Service NSW Centre?
faqs.a: You may be required to visit a Service NSW Centre to have your photo taken.
